claims.text: Classic cystitis in a young, healthy woman without red flags is often treated presumptively without testing.
claims.quote: Many clinicians presumptively give antibiotics for cystitis without any testing (sometimes not even urinalysis) in young, otherwise healthy women presenting with classic dysuria, frequency, and urgency and without red flag findings.

claims.text: Clean-catch midstream urinalysis and culture; culture is recommended with risk factors for multidrug-resistant infection.
claims.quote: Others evaluate everyone with a clean-catch midstream urine sample for urinalysis and culture. Urine culture is recommended in patients with risk factors for multidrug-resistant infections.

claims.text: Pregnancy test in women of childbearing age; wet mount for vaginal discharge.
claims.quote: In women of childbearing age, a pregnancy test is done (UTI during pregnancy is of concern because it may increase the risk of preterm labor or premature rupture of the membranes). Vaginal discharge warrants a wet mount.

claims.text: STI testing (gonococcus and chlamydia culture or PCR) of cervical or urethral exudate, since many infected patients present atypically.
claims.quote: Many clinicians routinely obtain samples of cervical (women) or urethral (men) exudate for STI testing (gonococcus and chlamydia culture or polymerase chain reaction [PCR]) because many infected patients do not have a typical presentation.

claims.text: WBCs with a sterile culture are nonspecific: STI, vulvovaginitis, prostatitis, TB, tumor or interstitial nephritis.
claims.quote: WBCs detected with urinalysis in patients with sterile cultures are nonspecific and may occur with an STI, vulvovaginitis, prostatitis, tuberculosis (TB), tumor, interstitial nephritis, or other causes.

claims.text: Cystoscopy and urinary tract imaging for no response to antibiotics, recurrent symptoms, or hematuria without infection.
claims.quote: Cystoscopy and imaging of the urinary tract may be indicated to check for obstruction, anatomic abnormalities, cancer, or other problems in patients who have no response to antibiotics, recurrent symptoms, or hematuria without infection.
